SUBJECT:  A Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for
  periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration at 415 Alta Vista
  (PC#2888)
________________________________________________________________________

SUMMARY: A Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development
Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30)
consecutive days duration in the Low Density Residential (LD) zone at 415 Alta Vista. The
Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 - Existing Facilities). The proposed project is not
located within the appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find this project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 under Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, because it
  has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 25-55 approving a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit pursuant to PC#2888 (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a
authorize the Planning Commission to review and take action on applications for a Transient
Rental License and Coastal Development Permit.

BACKGROUND:

Application Information:

  Applicant  Robert and Christy Hyer
  Owner  Catalina Getaway LLC
  Location  415 Alta Vista
  APN  7480-047-092
  General Plan  Low Density Residential
  Land Use Designation
  Zoning Classification  Low Density Residential (LD)
  File Date  8/1/2023

65059.00002\44376759.1
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 2

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel addressed 415 Alta Vista. The parcel is
situated between Mar de Cortez to the north and Alta Vista to the south. The lot slopes
dramatically to the northeast towards the coastline.

The project site is currently developed with a 10,268 square foot, three-story residence with
multiple exterior decks facing the coastline. Completed in 2025, the residence has not been
significantly modified since it was finaled.

All abutting properties are in the LD zone and represent a mix of single-family residential villas
and residential condominiums within Hamilton Cove. A vicinity map, including adjacent property
types and existing short-term rental status, is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

The project site has not been granted any previous entitlements.

There are no active or recent building permits for this property.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicants, Robert and Christy Hyer, propose to short-term rent
portions of the main and lower levels of the single-family residence at 415 Alta Vista. Transient
renters would have access to:
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 3

  •  Main (2nd) Floor – Garage (including golf cart) and three bedrooms.
  •  Lower (1st) Floor – Three bedrooms, common room, laundry room, kitchenette, game
  room, outdoor bbq area, and balcony.

Transient renters would not have access to the upper (3rd) floor (master bedroom suite), nor the
kitchen, living room, pantry, dining room, balconies, or pool on the main (2nd) floor. These areas
will be locked when transient renters are on the property and will remain for use by the property
owner only.

The maximum occupancy of the rentable area of the residence will be fourteen (14) individuals
based on the bedroom count and license limitations set forth in AMC Section 3-1.317.g.

The transient rental application and proposed rental floor plan are included in Attachments 3
and 4 of this report.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: Staff has identified two issue items for discussion regarding the
proposed project related to the use of the exterior decks.

Issue 1: Exterior Deck and Balcony

The subject property has an exterior deck and balcony that will be accessible to transient renters.
Exterior decks are common within the Hamilton Cove development, as units are designed to
take advantage of the sweeping views of the coastline in the area. Nuisance noise is generally
a concern for residents of any residential area. The villas area of Hamilton Cove is not as densely
developed as the condominium area, but there is potential for sound to travel due to the
geography of the development.

The property is located within Noise District 2. This is the district assignment for commercial
areas or other areas not depicted on AMC Section 5-13.04 Table 2. AMC Section 5-13.08.a.2.a
prohibits the operation of sound amplifying equipment outdoors in such a manner as to be plainly
audible from the real property line of which the sound amplifying equipment is located, absent
approval of a Special Use Permit.

AMC 3-1.317 provides standard conditions which are applicable to all transient rental and
incorporated into the draft resolution. Two conditions prohibit the use of unenclosed balconies
and patios between the hours of 9:00 PM and 8:00 AM (Condition #8) and also require that all
transient rentals comply with the noise regulations set for in AMC Chapter 5-13, Noise (Condition
#9).

Furthermore, transient guests will only have access to the outdoor pool area and large deck on
the main level of the building, which comprises the largest outdoor gathering area in the
residence.

Therefore, it is the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions adequately
address potential nuisance noise concerns related to the exterior decks and no additional
conditions are required to meet the findings required to grant a TRL for the property.
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 4

Issue 2: Maximum Rental Occupancy

The maximum occupancy of the unit will be fourteen (14) individuals based on the bedroom
count and license limitations set forth in AMC Section 3-1.317.g., which is two individuals per
bedroom plus two additional persons.

Pursuant to standard Condition #7 of the draft resolution, the Planning Commission may
establish a different maximum occupancy number, if justified by the facts in the record. This may
be done when appropriate and reasonable, for example, in the presence of unique site
characteristics of the property. Reasons for establishing a different maximum occupancy number
include, but are not limited to:

  a. Size and location of the property;
  b. Distinction between single- and multi-unit properties; and
  c. Number and size of each sleeping room in the transient rental unit

The fourteen person maximum occupancy is a relatively large number of people compared to
the standard single-family residence. However, the residence itself includes a large number of
interior living areas and amenities that are not otherwise found in other neighborhoods within the
city. Therefore, staff does not recommend any additional conditions further limiting the maximum
occupancy of the transient rental.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Transient Rental License
The proposed project may be granted a Transient Rental License for short-term rental per AMC
Chapter 3-1 (Business Licensing) Article 3 (Transient Rental Licenses). AMC Section 3-1.310
sets forth the required findings for approval of a Transient Rental License as follows:

  a) The Planning Commission may, with such conditions as are deemed necessary, approve
  a Transient Rental License which will not jeopardize, adversely affect, endanger or
  otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general welfare, or be
  materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the vicinity of such use.

  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. Staff has added two
  additional conditions, Conditions #12 and 13, to clarify the portion of the residence that is
  licensed for transient rental and that a security plan shall be maintained on file with the
  Planning and Building Department which shows how the non-rental areas of the
  residence will be secured for safety of transient guests.

  b) In making such determination, the Planning Commission shall find that the proposed
  transient rental use is in general accord with the following principles and standards:

  1)  The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings and structures
  shall be considered and no proposed transient rental use shall be permitted where
  such use will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses,
  buildings and structures;
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 5

  The subject property is an existing single-family residence located within the villas
  area of Hamilton Cove. No modifications to the property are proposed that would
  alter the ability of the building to function as a single-family residence in the future.
  The property was inspected by the Planning and Building Department prior to the
  public hearing and no health and safety issues were identified by the inspector that
  would prevent the residence from being used as a transient rental. Standard and
  recommended conditions of approval will ensure that operation of the transient
  rental will remain orderly and not have an adverse effect on surrounding residential
  properties.

2)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be adequate in size and shape
  to accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities,
  landscaping, outdoor entertaining areas and other development features
  prescribed in this chapter or as required as a condition in order to integrate said
  use and not be detrimental with the uses in the neighborhood;

  The subject property is an existing three-story single-family residence. Transient
  renters would have access to the following areas of the residence:

  •  Main (2nd) Floor – Garage (including golf cart) and three bedrooms.
  •  Lower (1st) Floor – Three bedrooms, common room, laundry room,
  kitchenette, game room, outdoor bbq area, and balcony.

  Transient renters would not have access to the upper (3rd) floor (master bedroom
  suite), nor the kitchen, living room, pantry, dining room, balconies, or pool on the
  main (2nd) floor. These areas will be locked when transient renters are on the
  property and will remain for use by the property owner only.

  The property will offer a vehicle for transient rental guests, which has a designated
  garage parking space.

3)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be served by highways and
  streets adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity
  of traffic such use would generate.

  The project site is located between Mar de Cortez and Alta Vista within the
  Hamilton Cove residential development. Hamilton Cove is a gated community, with
  access only granted to residents and guests, which limits the amount of pedestrian
  and vehicular traffic to the area. St. Catherine Way, the only road access from
  Hamilton Cove to the city center, is not identified as a Major Circulation Facility in
  the General Plan Circulation Element. A vehicle will be provided for transient
  guests, which will ensure that transient guests will have adequate access to
  amenities and services within the city center of Avalon.

4)  That the transient rental use must be ancillary to the residential use of residential
  unit, and would not create a commercial use in a residential zone. Whether a use
  is for a commercial use may be determined by the number of transient rental
  licenses previously granted to the applicant, the applicant's reason for the license
  and the nature of the requested license and any other factors presented in the
  application or at the hearing.
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 6

  The applicant currently does not any other transient rentals within the city. The
  residence recently received certificate of occupancy and will be used for short-term
  rentals if the license is granted. No modifications are proposed to the residence
  that would intensify the use of the property or alter the ability of the residence to
  function as a single-family residence in the future.

c) Conditions imposed by the Planning Commission for a Transient Rental License may
  involve any pertinent factors affecting the establishment, operation and maintenance of
  the requested transient rental use, including, but not limited to:

  1) Special yards, open spaces and buffer areas;
  2) Fences and walls;
  3) Parking facilities, including vehicular ingress and egress and the surfacing of parking
  area and driveways to specified standards;
  4) Street and highway dedications and improvements including sidewalks, curbs and
  gutters;
  5) Water supply and fire protection;
  6) Landscaping and maintenance of grounds;
  7) Regulation of nuisance factors such as noise, vibrations, smoke, dust, dirt, odors,
  gases, noxious matter, heat, glare, electromagnetic disturbances and radiation;
  8) Regulation of operating hours for activities affecting normal neighborhood schedules
  and functions;
  9) Regulation of signs, including outdoor advertising; and
  10) Such other conditions as will make possible the development of the proposed
  transient rental use in an orderly and efficient manner and in general accord with all
  elements of the General Plan and the intent and purpose of this chapter.

  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. Additional special
  conditions #12 and 13 have been included in order to clarify the area of the residence
  that will be rented transiently, and to require a security plan to ensure the safety of
  transient guests.

d) The Planning Commission shall deny the requested Transient Rental License where:

  1) The findings indicate, and the Commission determines, that the applicant has failed
  to show that the requested transient rental use will not jeopardize, adversely affect.
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use, and reasonable restrictions or conditions to license the
  establishment of the proposed use will not prevent detriment or menace as indicated.

  Pursuant to AMC Section 3-1.310.a-c, the required findings have been made to
  determine that the proposed transient rental will not jeopardize, adversely affect,
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use. Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set
  forth in AMC Section 3-1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project.
  Additional special conditions #12 and 13 have been included in order to clarify the
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 7

  area of the residence that will be rented transiently, and to require a security plan to
  ensure the safety of transient guests.

  2) The applicant fails to attend the hearing of the Planning Commission in person or
  virtually, unless a valid excuse is provided.

  The applicant confirmed with Staff their intent to be in attendance at the public hearing
  prior to the publication of the meeting agenda.

  3) The applicant has previously had a Transient Rental License revoked for failure to
  maintain such license in good standing or for violation of the Municipal Code or any
  condition of the permit or had a conditional use permit revoked for violation of any
  requirement of this Municipal Code or violation of any condition of approval of the
  permit.

  The applicant has not had a business license, conditional use permit, or transient
  rental license for transient occupancy in the past, nor had any such license revoked
  for violations of the Municipal Code.

  4) The applicant previously operated a transient rental without a Transient Rental
  License. In deciding whether to deny the Transient Rental License on this basis, the
  Planning Commission may determine, in its reasonable discretion, whether
  substantial evidence supports that the applicant was not acting in bad faith when
  engaging in an illegal transient rental operation based upon: (1) the length of time that
  the operator failed to obtain a valid transient rental, (2) the length of time between
  when the operator was notified of the illegal operation and the time when the operator
  applied for a license, (3) whether the operator immediately discontinued illegal
  transient rental operation upon notice, (4) whether only one transient rental unit was
  operated, and (5) whether the operator was a sophisticated party, meaning the
  operator or its affiliates have engaged in transient rental operation previously. The
  applicant has the burden of presenting evidence that prior illegal transient rental
  operation was not conducted deliberately or in bad faith.

  The applicant has not previously operated a transient rental without a license within
  the city.

  5) The property proposed for transient rental use is out of compliance with any
  requirement of this Municipal Code at the time the Planning Commission hears the
  application.

  The project site is not subject to any active code enforcement cases and is otherwise
  in good standing with licensing and permitting requirements with the City of Avalon.

e) In addition to the foregoing, the Planning Commission shall consider the following in
  connection with an application for a Transient Rental License:

  1) Year-Round Rental Status. In the absence of adequate mitigating measures proposed
  by the applicant, the application should be denied where the subject property is or has
  been rented for periods of more than 30 consecutive days to the same occupant at
  any time during the two years preceding the application.
   PC#2888 – 415 Alta Vista
  Page 8

  Staff has found no evidence that the subject property has been rented for 30
  consecutive days or more to the same occupant in the last two years. The property
  has recently received certificate of occupancy has not been occupied prior to the
  public hearing.

2) Neighborhood Impacts. The Planning Commission shall consider the objections of the
  owners and occupants of neighboring properties in determining whether the proposed
  transient rental use is consistent with the surrounding properties and the extent to
  which such impacts may be mitigated by the imposition of the standard conditions
  listed below or by the imposition of additional conditions. The Planning Commission
  may consider objections previously made in connection with applications for transient
  rental use at other properties located within the same general area as the subject
  application; however, the Planning Commission should consider the time between the
  prior application and the subject application, the geographical proximity of the subject
  application to the prior application, any differing circumstances, and additional
  mitigating measures proposed by the applicant, and changes in the general area, in
  determining the weight to be given such prior objections.

  No objection letters were received by the Planning and Building Department prior to
  the publication of the meeting agenda.

3) Condominium Associations Having IO or More Units. In the case of an application
  concerning property located within a condominium or similar congregate housing

since completion.

All abutting properties to the north, east, and south are in the HD zone and represent a mix of
one- and two-story residential buildings and commercial hotels. The Vons grocery store, located
to the west, is zoned Commercial. A vicinity map, including adjacent property types and existing
short-term rental status, is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

bedroom, three bathroom unit in a three unit building (duplex with ADU). The residence has one
bedroom and a kitchen on the first floor, three bedrooms on the second floor, and a porch and
balcony facing Catalina Avenue. The entire unit will be rented as a single rental, while the ADU
(first floor) and Unit B (second floor) will remain and year-round rentals. Short-term rental guests

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: Staff has identified two issue items for discussion regarding the
proposed project related to adjacent short-term rentals and the open porch and balcony.

Issue 1: Adjacent Short-term Rentals

AMC Section 3-1.310.3.4 states that the Planning Commission shall consider whether granting
the Transient Rental License shall result in any year round residence located adjacent to the
proposed transient rental having more than a majority of the adjacent residences permitted or
licensed for transient rental use.

The vicinity map prepared for the project, included as Attachment 2 of the staff report, shows
that granting of the transient rental license at the subject property will result in one property, 241
Descanso Avenue, having more than a majority of the adjacent residences permitted or licensed
for transient rental use, with transient rentals on three or four sides.

241 Descanso Avenue is a single-family residence. No evidence is available in city records that
indicates whether this unit is utilized as an owner-occupied residence, vacation home, or year
round rental. The residence is located within the SC zone, which is zoned for a mix of residential
and commercial uses, with higher intensity of use than surrounding residential zones. The
residence will be buffered from the transient rental at 240 Catalina Avenue by the two year-round
rentals at the rear of the building. 236 Catalina Avenue, a grandfathered short-term rental, is
also currently owner-occupied.

Therefore, it is the opinion of staff that the granting of the transient rental for 240 Catalina Avenue
Unit A is consistent with the intent of the zone, and that the circumstances of adjacent residences
are not sufficient to justify denial of the TRL application.

Issue 2: Unenclosed Porch, Balcony, and Roof Deck

Unit A has an unenclosed porch on the first floor, a balcony on the second floor, and a roof deck,
all of which will be accessible to transient renters. While porches, balconies, and roof decks are
common in the area, nuisance noise is generally a concern for residents who reside in the Flats,
as residences are situated closely together and the acoustics of the area allow for sound to travel
far distances throughout the neighborhood.

The property is located within Noise District 3, which is characterized as a mix of residential and
commercial uses. AMC Section 5-13.08.a.2.a prohibits the operation outdoors of any radio

of the building. The unit has two bedrooms, two bathrooms and a kitchen on the first level and

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: Staff has identified one issue item for discussion regarding the
proposed project related to the use of the unenclosed deck.

Issue 1: Unenclosed Deck

The subject unit has an existing unenclosed deck on the first level of the unit, which will be
accessible to transient renters. The deck is not shared with other units in the building. While
decks are common in the area, nuisance noise is generally a concern for residents who reside
in the city center, as residences are situated closely together and the acoustics of the area allow
for sound to travel far distances throughout the neighborhood. This particular area on Metropole
Avenue is density developed with multi-family buildings, and the deck for the unit faces north
towards the Cameron Hotel site (301 Beacon Street) and the Beacon Hill Senior Apartments.

The property is located within Noise District 3, which is characterized as a mix of residential and
commercial uses. AMC Section 5-13.08.a.2.a prohibits the operation outdoors of any radio
receiving set, sound amplifying equipment, television set, or other machine or device which
produces or reproduces sound in such a manner as to be plainly audible from the real property
line on which the sound amplifying equipment is located unless permitted by Special Use Permit.

Additionally, AMC 3-1.317 provides standard conditions which are applicable to all transient
rental and incorporated into the draft resolution. Two conditions prohibit the use of unenclosed
balconies and patios between the hours of 9:00 PM and 8:00 AM (Condition #8) and also require
that all transient rentals comply with the noise regulations set for in AMC Chapter 5-13, Noise
(Condition #9).

Therefore, it is the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions adequately
address potential nuisance noise concerns related to the roof deck and no additional conditions
are required to meet the findings required to grant a TRL for the property.

  c. Name of the managing agency, agent, property manager, or owner of the unit, and
  a local telephone number at which that property manager or his agent may be
  reached on a twenty-four-hour basis; and
  d. City of Avalon Business License Number

3. Advertising Requirements. Any sign or online posting advertising the available use of a
  transient rental unit must meet all of the advertising and sign requirements found in the
  Avalon Municipal Code, including identification of the property's City of Avalon Business
  License Number.

4. Notice and Rental Agreement Requirements.

  a. Upon check-in, the managing agency, agent, property manager, owner of the unit
  or other designee must meet all transient rental guests in person prior to providing
  access to the property to review rental regulations and verify the number of guests
  arriving are in compliance with the unit's occupancy limits.

  12
   i. The managing agency, agent, property manager, owner of the unit or other
  designee must maintain a valid City of Avalon Business License.

  b. Each transient rental unit shall have a clearly visible and legible notice posted
  within the unit on or adjacent to the front door, containing the following
  information:

  i. The name of the managing agency, agent, property manager, or owner of
  the unit, and a local telephone number at which that party or his/her agent
  may be reached on a twenty-four-hour basis;
  ii. The maximum number of occupants permitted to stay in the unit;
  iii. Notification that trash and refuse shall not be left or stored on the property,
  the scheduled dates and times for pick-up at the location, and an explanation
  of the City's recycling program;
  iv. Notification that failure to conform to the parking and occupancy
  requirements of the structure is a violation of this section;
  v. When the City has enacted water conservancy measures by ordinance,
  notice of the requirements of such ordinance and a request that occupants
  conserve water as much as possible in the use of showers, baths, faucets and
  laundry;
  vi. Notification that use of unenclosed decks and patios between 9:00 p.m. and
  8:00 a.m. is prohibited where such use generates noise which would disturb
  or annoy a reasonable person occupying the adjacent properties; and
  vii. A statement that Avalon has a "zero tolerance" policy towards nuisances,
  rowdy and disruptive behavior and advising that the occupancy will be
  immediately terminated for violations of this policy.

  c. The foregoing information shall be stated in the rental information and agreement
  provided to prospective renters prior to their occupancy of the unit.

5. Vehicles. Off-street parking shall be provided on or off site such that all vehicles bearing
  permits issued for the unit can be parked off street, except when used pursuant to a
  temporary permit issued to the owner as provided in Title 4. The owner, agent and
  managing agency shall comply with the Avalon vehicle ordinance which (I) permits
  transient renters to only use the vehicle which is permitted for the location; and (2) prohibits
  the owner, agent or managing agency from charging for the use of the vehicle, except:

  a. Properties located in the "flats" (as defined in§ 9-5.406) and properties located in
  the condominium known as "Bahia Vista," "Canyon Terrace," and "Sol Vista" shall
  not include a vehicle to be used by transient guests.

6. Trash. The owner or managing agent shall provide written information to each transient
  occupant setting out the schedule for trash pick-up at the location and an explanation of the
  City's recycling program and ensure that there are adequate materials for disposing of trash
  in accordance with the City's program. All trash containers shall be secured against animal
  incursion.

  13
 7. Maximum Occupancy. The maximum occupancy for transient rentals shall be two persons
  (including children and infants) per bedroom, plus two; provided the Planning Commission
  in its discretion may establish a different maximum number where appropriate and
  reasonable to permit fewer persons that the foregoing formula might otherwise allow and
  may also increase the number that would otherwise be allowed under the foregoing formula
  where facts are presented demonstrating that the configuration of the property warrants it.
  Reasons for establishing a different maximum occupancy number include, but are not
  limited to:

  a. Size and location of the property;
  b. Distinction between single- and multi-unit properties; and
  c. Number and size of each sleeping room in the transient rental unit

8. Unenclosed Areas. The use of unenclosed areas, such as decks and balconies, attached to
  each transient rental unit shall be prohibited between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.
  Monday through Sunday.

9. Noise. The occupants of the transient rental shall at all times remain in compliance with
  the Noise Ordinance as outlined in Chapter 5-13 of this Municipal Code.

10. Code Compliance, Fire Safety and Inspection. Each dwelling unit used for transient rental
  within the City is subject to all of the following inspection requirements:

  a. The owner shall be responsible for compliance with all codes regarding Fire,
  Building and Safety, Health and Safety and other relevant laws and the
  requirements of these Conditions of Approval.

  b. The transient rental unit shall be inspected prior to commencement of the use,
  which inspection shall be scheduled and conducted within 30 days of approval. In
  addition to the registration for each unit as required in subsection (a) of this section,
  an original, signed inspection report for each unit shall be submitted to the Director
  of Finance in order to obtain approval to use the unit as a transient rental.
  Inspections shall be conducted by a qualified inspector(s) authorized and approved
  by the City to conduct such inspections. Inspectors shall demonstrate appropriate
  qualifications to conduct the required inspections as determined by the Building
  Official or the Fire Department, as applicable. The cost of such inspections, plus
  any administrative charges shall be paid by the owner pursuant to the City's adopted
  fee schedule. The City shall make every reasonable effort to ensure that inspections
  are completed in a timely manner. Within 15 days following inspection, the
  inspectors shall submit an original, signed inspection report to the Planning
  Department, or, where applicable, provide notice that the property owner has
  unreasonably prevented inspection. Failure to cooperate with the scheduling of
  inspection shall subject the approval to use the unit as a transient rental to
  revocation.

  14
 c. After the initial inspection, each rental unit shall be reinspected no less than once
  every three years following the original inspection. Verification of inspection will
  be done at the time of business license renewal. Failure to submit inspection reports
  shall result in revocation of approval to use the unit for transient rentals.

d. Inspections shall verify compliance with all applicable provisions of this section.

e. If upon completing an inspection of a transient rental, the inspector(s) determines
  that the unit is not in conformance with this section, the inspector shall provide the
  managing agency, agent, owner or prope1ty manager with a list of required
  corrections, set a reasonable time for correction and a date for reinspection. A copy
  of the foregoing shall also be given to the Planning Department. If the unit is
  registered with the City as a transient rental, approval by the City to use the unit for
  transient rental shall be suspended until correction and reinspection if determined
  by the inspector to present an immediate health and safety hazard, and submission
  of a new inspection report for the unit indicating compliance with this section. If
  the unit is not yet registered with or approved by the City, approval for its use as a
  transient rental shall be withheld until submission of a new inspection report for the
  unit indicating compliance with this section.

f. Noncompliance by an owner, managing agency, property manager or agent of the
  requirements for registration, inspection and operation of transient rentals may
  result in the revocation of the business license and Transient Rental License
  authorizing the use, and upon revocation, no new business license or Transient
  Rental License may be issued to the same transient rental licensee for a period of
  12 months following such revocation.

g. The following requirements for transient rentals will be evaluated upon inspection
  of each unit, and shall constitute minimum requirements. The unit must be brought
  into conformance with these requirements and any other applicable codes and
  ordinances in order for the use to be allowed.

  i. Required sign and notice must be posted, and address of unit must be legible
  from outside the property unless exempted.
  ii. Smoke detectors shall be installed within each sleeping room and at a point
  centrally located in the corridor or area giving access to each separate
  sleeping room. Battery-operated smoke detectors are acceptable, provided
  that they are maintained in good working order at all times, or except as
  required by other applicable codes. Where fire suppression systems have
  been installed, such systems shall also be subject to the inspection and
  testing requirements set forth in Title 4, Chapter 3.
  iii. The transient rental shall be equipped with a minimum of one 2A: I 0B:C
  type extinguisher with 75 feet of travel distance to all portions of the
  structure; there shall be no less than one such extinguisher per floor. Fire
  extinguishers shall be mounted in visible locations with the tops of the

  15
   extinguishers mounted between three feet and five feet above the floor and
  shall be accessible to occupants at all times. California State Fire Marshal
  annual certification tags must be provided and be current on all
  extinguishers.
  iv. Any locking mechanism on outside doors must be operable from inside the
  unit without the use of a key. If the dwelling unit is greater than 3,000 square
  feet in area, two exit doors shall be required, each of which shall conform
  to this requirement.
  v. Transient rentals shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition and
  free from hazards, which shall include meeting the following requirements:
  1. There shall be no exposed wiring, improper wiring materials, or
  overloaded electrical circuits;
  2. There shall be no permanent use of extension cords for appliances,
  heaters, lamps or other fixtures;
  3. There shall be no leaking fixtures, clogged or leaking wastewater
  lines;
  4. Faucets and fixtures shall be maintained in working conditions;
  5. Showers, sinks and bathing facilities shall be clean and properly
  maintained;
  6. There shall be no evidence of pest infestations;
  7. If directed by the Fire Department, bedroom windows shall be
  operable to allow for emergency egress:
  8. There shall be at least one window per bedroom, to allow for proper
  interior ventilation;
  9. There shall be no accumulation of trash and/or debris on the site or
  within the unit;
  10. All steps, stairways, decks and railings shall be stable and
  structurally sound;
  11. All standard appliances, including but not limited to kitchen
  appliances, furnaces and water heaters, shall be operational;
  12. Any hot tubs, pools and spas shall be fenced or equipped with an
  approved cover with locking mechanisms as required by State law,
  and shall be maintained in a safe and sanitary condition;
  13. Any lofts or attic conversions shall be provided with acceptable
  exiting and head clearance; stairs or providing access to these areas
  shall be safe and structurally sound; and
  14. Exits shall remain clear of storage, debris or impedance at all times.

h. The managing agency, agent, property manager, or owner of the unit whose name
  and local telephone number appears on the sign pursuant to subsection (b) of this
  section or pursuant to a conditional use permit and/or who is identified in the
  Transient Rental License must maintain a physical presence within the
  geographical limits of the City of Avalon during the term of the transient rental unit
  lease in order to provide response to complaints within 30 minutes of notification.
  Failure to be available or failure to answer the telephone shall be deemed the same
  as failure to respond.

  16
 11. Annual Minimum Stay. Any managing agency, agent, owner or property manager who
  rents one or more transient rentals shall be required to ensure a minimum stay of at least
  ten (10) nights in each transient rental per calendar year.
